I found no dated AI predictions by Mark Zuckerberg from 2020. All three fixed searches ran, and I opened four 2020 sources: the Silicon Slopes interview and three earnings calls. None had a forward-looking AI claim tied to a date or span. A fifth source, the Munich Security Conference transcript, wouldn't open, so I haven't checked it.

- **His 2020 forecasts weren't about AI.** His January 2020 decade post predicted "breakthrough augmented reality glasses" in the 2020s, but I saw that only in search snippets. At Silicon Slopes (January 31, 2020) he said "the craziest" thing coming "in the next 10 years" was "real, true, augmented reality and a more mainstream virtual reality." On the Q3 2020 call he set a goal of 10 million active VR units. Those are product forecasts, not AI, so they're left out.
- **His 2020 AI remarks look back, not forward.** On the Q2 2020 call he said Facebook had "become a pioneer in using artificial intelligence to remove hateful content at scale." That describes the past and gives no date.
- **Not checked:** the Munich talk (February 2020), where coverage says he spoke about finding harmful content proactively. The Marquette archive page loaded, but the PDF link returned "not accessible." I also didn't reach the June 2020 town-hall video, the Facebook Connect 2020 keynote or the Q4 2019 call (held January 2020). I had no page openings left.
- **Search budget:** I used 9 of the 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
- **Other years:** two search snippets pointed to AI remarks on calls from other years (Q4 2017 and Q3 2019). I didn't open either page, so treat them as leads only.
